quotes: He presented at 4 months with enlarged knees that could not fully extend, while his length (−0.5 SDS) and head circumference (+0.5 SDS) were normal.
A homozygous g.122839967G>A (Chr7[GRCh37]), c.34C>T, p.(Arg12Ter) variant was identified in the first exon of the SLC13A1 gene (NM_022444.3).

The patient had a 20 Mb region‐of‐homozygosity on chromosome 7q31.32 containing both the SLC13A1 and the CFTR gene, while his parents were heterozygous for both variants, suggesting a common ancestor.

records.label: Proband 5
quotes: Proband 5 is a male and only child of healthy, nonconsanguineous parents who presented with concern for scoliosis at 14 years of age.
Growth parameters were notable for proportionate short stature (157.3 cm, 1.7th percentile, z = −2.13) with normal weight (59 kg, 39th percentile, z = −0.27).

notes.statement: Tise et al. (2025) described 5 children from 4 families with biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC13A1 who presented with concern for short stature and were found to have scoliosis and/or skeletal dysplasia. Reduced plasma sulfate and/or increased urinary sulfate excretion was found in both probands tested.
quotes: All probands presented with concern for short stature and were found to have scoliosis and/or skeletal dysplasia. A reduction in plasma sulfate level and/or increase in urinary sulfate excretion was detected in 2 of 2 probands evaluated.

notes.statement: Tise et al. (2025) noted that all SLC13A1 variants in their cohort showed biallelic inheritance, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: All SLC13A1 variants demonstrated biallelic inheritance, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance, and resulted in missense or nonsense changes.

notes.statement: Tise et al. (2025) found that the SLC13A1 missense variants R237C, G448D, L516P, and Y582H expressed in stably transfected MDCK cells showed no detectable [35S]-sulfate transport compared with wildtype, although plasma membrane localization was similar to wildtype, suggesting the substitutions affect transport rather than trafficking.
quotes: All 4 amino acid sequence substitutions, p.(Arg237Cys), p.(Gly448Asp), p.(Leu516Pro), and p.(Tyr582His), led to complete loss of sulfate transport activity because no detectable [35S]-sulfate transport was present for mutants compared with the control wild-type mEmerald-SLC13A1 construct (Figure 4A).
suggesting that these amino acid substitutions affect sulfate transport but do not appear to completely disrupt trafficking to the plasma membrane.

notes.statement: Using a homology model of SLC13A1 based on the SLC13A5 structure, Tise et al. (2025) predicted that the missense substitutions disrupt contacts and hydrogen bonds or introduce clashes in transmembrane helices (TM5, TM9, TM10) or the extracellular C terminus, which may impair transport.
quotes: The p.(Leu516Pro) substitution (L516P) is predicted to remove most of these contacts and introduce clashes with the backbone of the helix at P512 and L513 (Figure 3F).
The p.(Gly448Asp) substitution (G448D) is predicted to introduce a new contact with C37 in TM2, and introduce significant clashes with L66 and M72 (Figure 3D).

notes.statement: Tise et al. (2025) noted that the G448D, L516P, and Y582H variants were absent in homozygous state from gnomAD v4.1.0, with heterozygous allele counts of 221, 7, and 3, respectively.
quotes: Homozygous missense variants were absent from the Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD v4.1.0) for variants NM_022444.4: c.1343G>A p.(Gly448Asp), NM_022444.4:c.1547T>C p.(Leu516Pro) and NM_022444.4:c.1744T>C p.(Tyr582His), with heterozygous allele counts of 221, 7, and 3, respectively.

notes.statement: Tise et al. (2025) noted that the patient homozygous for the W48X nonsense variant had a neurodevelopmental phenotype, and that whether SLC13A1 loss-of-function variants, or possibly only nonsense variants, are associated with neurodevelopmental features requires further study.
quotes: Whether SLC13A1 LOF variants or possibly only nonsense variants, are associated with a neurodevelopmental phenotype will require identification and evaluation of additional individuals.

notes.statement: Tise et al. (2025) suggested that oral sulfate supplementation, directly or via sources such as N-acetyl-L-cysteine, warrants evaluation, and advised caution in giving acetaminophen and other drugs metabolized by sulfation to individuals with biallelic SLC13A1 loss-of-function variants.
quotes: The use of oral sulfate supplementation, either directly or via other sulfate sources, such as NAC, to saturate other collateral sulfate transporters and any residual SLC13A1 function is an approach that warrants further evaluation in humans.

caution should be taken in the administration and dosing of acetaminophen and other medications metabolized via sulfation to individuals with biallelic SLC13A1 LOF variants until the full clinical phenotype is better understood.

notes.statement: Tise et al. (2025) recommended sulfate measurement in plasma and urine to aid interpretation of SLC13A1 variants and the addition of SLC13A1 to short stature, scoliosis, and skeletal dysplasia gene panels.
quotes: Sulfate measurements should be considered in the clinical interpretation of variants identified in SLC13A1.
This work provides strong support for the addition of SLC13A1 to short stature, scoliosis, and skeletal dysplasia gene panels

notes.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) found a fractional sulfate excretion close to 100% in the patient (reference 13-34%), consistent with complete loss of renal sulfate reabsorption, and an over 80% reduction in plasma sulfate. Heterozygous parents had plasma sulfate below the control range, and the mother had an FEsulfate of 45%.
quotes: We found an FEsulfate close to 100%, consistent with complete loss of renal sulfate reabsorption in our patient, as well as an over 80% reduction in plasma sulfate levels.
Plasma sulfate levels were severely reduced in the patient and also below the control range in both parents (Figure 2 and Table S1).

notes.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) found that the percentage of chondroitin sulfate disaccharides in urinary glycosaminoglycans was not significantly different in the patient compared with parents and controls. Serum cholesterol sulfate was reduced, whereas other steroid sulfates were normal.
quotes: The percentage chondroitin sulfate disaccharides in urinary glycosaminoglycans did not differ significantly in the patient, the parents and the controls (Table S2).
Serum cholesterol sulfate was reduced in the patient (443 ng/ml; reference range 500–1236 ng/ml), while other serum steroid sulfates were within the reference range (Table S3).

notes.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) found that intravenous N-acetylcysteine normalized plasma sulfate in the patient, but levels returned to baseline 15 hours after the infusion stopped. Because of a possible increased risk of acetaminophen hepatotoxicity, the patient was advised to avoid acetaminophen.
quotes: Plasma sulfate concentrations normalized after bolus injection of NAC and during maintenance infusion but returned to baseline 15 h after stop of the infusion (Figure 4).
Although the patient's transaminase levels were normal on multiple occasions, he has been strongly advised to avoid acetaminophen.

notes.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) noted that the spondylo-epi-metaphyseal radiologic abnormalities seen early in life improved with age. By age 11 years, only flattening of the cervical vertebral bodies and irregular lumbar endplates remained.
quotes: The radiological abnormalities ameliorated and at 11 years, only flattening of the cervical vertebral bodies and irregular lumbar vertebral endplates remained (Figure 1C).

notes.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) noted relatively high global allele frequencies for the SLC13A1 loss-of-function variants Arg12Ter (0.20%) and Trp48Ter (0.05%), with 1 Arg12Ter homozygote in gnomAD. They hypothesized that biallelic loss-of-function variants are more common than recognized and may present later in life with degenerative bone and joint disease.
quotes: In fact, two SLC13A1 loss‐of‐function variants, Arg12Ter and Trp48Ter, have a relatively high global allele frequencies (0.20% and 0.05%, respectively) and homozygosity for the Arg12Ter SLC13A1 variant is reported once in the Genome Aggregation Database
We hypothesize that biallelic SLC13A1 loss‐of‐function variants are more common and may also present later in life with degenerative bone and joint disease

notes.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) noted that the SLC13A1 Arg12Ter variant had previously been shown to cause total loss of function in Xenopus laevis oocytes.
quotes: This variant causes a gain of stop predicted to result in a truncated protein and has previously been shown to cause total loss‐of‐function in Xenopus laevis oocytes.
